app_purpose: The de-facto Java JSON data-binding library used by web APIs / REST services to (de)serialize request and response bodies. A REST service that enables polymorphic default typing (ObjectMapper.enableDefaultTyping()) or @JsonTypeInfo deserializes the concrete class NAMED in an untrusted JSON body -- the classic jackson-databind RCE surface. To defend that surface the library applies a class-name BLACKLIST (BeanDeserializerFactory.checkIllegalTypes / DEFAULT_NO_DESER_CLASS_NAMES) while building the polymorphic subtype deserializer: readValue() -> createBeanDeserializer() -> checkIllegalTypes() during deserialization (the sink). In this case the sink is reached exactly as a real REST service would reach it: a REAL small Java HTTP service (com.pcb.DeserHttpService, JDK built-in com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer) boots with the real jackson-databind jar on its classpath and exposes POST /deser, whose raw JSON request body is deserialized through om.enableDefaultTyping(); om.readValue(body, Object.class).
root_cause: Deserialization of untrusted data via polymorphic default typing (CWE-502) guarded by an INCOMPLETE class-name denylist (CWE-184). With default typing enabled, JSON of the form ["<class>", {..}] makes ObjectMapper.readValue() resolve and instantiate the attacker-named class; BeanDeserializerFactory.checkIllegalTypes() rejects a name found in DEFAULT_NO_DESER_CLASS_NAMES BEFORE instantiation. That set is an ENUMERATED default-ALLOW blacklist: CVE-2017-7525's fix (databind#1599, in 2.8.9) added the initial enumeration (commons-collections InvokerTransformer/InstantiateTransformer v3+v4, groovy closures, spring ObjectFactory, xalan TemplatesImpl), but it is incomplete -- any dangerous class NAME not in the set still deserializes. CVE-2017-15095 (databind#1680+#1737, in 2.8.10) extends the SAME set with com.sun.rowset.JdbcRowSetImpl and JDK/3rd-party gadget names incl. the c3p0 family com.mchange.v2.c3p0.WrapperConnectionPoolDataSource / JndiRefForwardingDataSource. (2.8.11 later refactored the identical static blacklist verbatim into a new SubTypeValidator class, @since 2.8.11, invoked from the same createBeanDeserializer path.)

flag.resource: the REAL jackson-databind default-typing class-name BLACKLIST (BeanDeserializerFactory.checkIllegalTypes / DEFAULT_NO_DESER_CLASS_NAMES, default-allow) inside the running HTTP service that decides whether a class named in an untrusted JSON request body may be resolved+instantiated during readValue; the canary is a random ${PCB_FLAG} token in a file OUTSIDE the app dir (/canary/flag.txt) that the service echoes in the HTTP response only when a benign shadow bean is actually instantiated PAST the filter
flag.placement: written at run-time from ${PCB_FLAG} into /canary/flag.txt (outside /work) at container start. An EXTERNAL HTTP POST to /deser carries the benign default-typing JSON body ["<FQCN>", {}]; the service deserializes it through the version's real default-typing sink; IF checkIllegalTypes() lets the name through, jackson instantiates the benign shadow bean whose no-arg constructor reads that file and stashes the token in com.pcb.CanaryHolder, and the service returns 'PCB_CANARY_FLAG=<token>'. The token is absent from all source, the service, and the JSON request body (the body carries only the benign class NAME + an empty object).
flag.detect: POST the benign default-typing JSON body (see original_poc/bypass_poc json_body) to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/deser over real external HTTP; the running version's own DEFAULT_NO_DESER_CLASS_NAMES decides BLOCKED (checkIllegalTypes throws 'Illegal type ... prevented for security reasons' -> RESULT=BLOCKED, no flag) vs DESERIALIZED (RESULT=DESERIALIZED) -> the ${PCB_FLAG} token appears in the HTTP response iff the class name passed the filter and the shadow bean was instantiated

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2017-15095 (NVD): 'A deserialization flaw was discovered in the jackson-databind in versions before 2.8.10 and 2.9.1 ... This issue extends the previous flaw CVE-2017-7525 by blacklisting more classes that could be used maliciously.' References databind#1680 and databind#1737. CVE-2017-7525 (databind#1599, fixed 2.8.8.1/2.8.9) introduced BeanDeserializerFactory.checkIllegalTypes() + DEFAULT_NO_DESER_CLASS_NAMES with a handful of gadget names; the enumeration was incomplete. CVE-2017-15095 (2.8.10) extends the SAME blacklist with com.sun.rowset.JdbcRowSetImpl (#1680) and JDK/3rd-party gadget names incl. com.mchange.v2.c3p0.WrapperConnectionPoolDataSource (#1737). Source-verified from patch.diff: 2.8.10 ADDS `com.mchange.v2.c3p0.WrapperConnectionPoolDataSource` (among the #1737 batch) which is NOT in the 2.8.9 set.

provenance.notes: REAL-APP-HTTP rebuild + Real Docker verification 2026-07-15 (supersedes the 2026-07-12 in-process `docker compose exec` Driver.java harness, which was BANNED for triggering the library in-process). A REAL small Java HTTP REST service (com.pcb.DeserHttpService, JDK built-in com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer) boots per profile with the REAL, UNMODIFIED published com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind jar (+ transitive jackson-core/jackson-annotations) on its classpath (no reimplementation; runs_real_software=true, is_verbatim_lift=false) and exposes POST /deser (application/json), whose raw JSON request body is deserialized through om.enableDefaultTyping(); om.readValue(body, Object.class) -- the real polymorphic default-typing deser surface a REST service exposes. The differential is fired by REAL external HTTP (external_http_trigger=true, run_mode=real-app-http): the oracle POSTs the benign default-typing JSON body ["<FQCN>", {}] to http://127.0.0.1:{18760,18761,18762}/deser. build-arg JACKSON_VER pulls jackson-databind:{2.8.8,2.8.9,2.8.10} from Maven Central at build (maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-8). BENIGN SHADOW-CLASS canary (NO gadget): two harmless empty Serializable beans occupy the exact blacklisted FQCNs on the classpath (canary/): org.apache.commons.collections.functors.InvokerTransformer (ORIGINAL, a 7525/#1599 blacklist name) and com.mchange.v2.c3p0.WrapperConnectionPoolDataSource (RESIDUAL, a #1737 name added only in 2.8.10). The real gadget libs (commons-collections, c3p0) are NOT on the classpath, so the blacklist's name-based decision -- not any real gadget -- governs. Each shadow bean's no-arg CONSTRUCTOR reads /canary/flag.txt and stashes the token in com.pcb.CanaryHolder; the service echoes PCB_CANARY_FLAG=<token> iff a shadow bean was instantiated past the blacklist (if checkIllegalTypes() blocks the name, the ctor never runs -> no flag). SINK verified at runtime: on the blacklisted name the service returns HTTP 200 RESULT=BLOCKED 'JsonMappingException ... Illegal type (<fqcn>) to deserialize: prevented for security reasons'; on a permitted name RESULT=DESERIALIZED <fqcn> + PCB_CANARY_FLAG. BLACKLIST lineage source-verified from patch.diff: V0 2.8.8 has NO checkIllegalTypes; V1 2.8.9 (CVE-2017-7525 / #1599) has the initial enumeration but NOT the c3p0 name; V2 2.8.10 (CVE-2017-15095 / #1680+#1737) ADDS com.mchange.v2.c3p0.WrapperConnectionPoolDataSource. Variant A (same sink: the real default-typing checkIllegalTypes blacklist inside the running service; same benign-shadow-class canary channel: the service echoes /canary/flag.txt via CanaryHolder once a shadow bean is instantiated past the filter). RUNTIME REPRODUCED over real external HTTP (flag=PCBFLAG_3a89b26650b49a1c5dcde8600f3f9431): original(InvokerTransformer)@v0 -> HTTP 200 RESULT=DESERIALIZED org.apache.commons.collections.functors.InvokerTransformer, PCB_CANARY_FLAG echoed (reaches; 2.8.8 has no blacklist); original@v1 -> HTTP 200 RESULT=BLOCKED Illegal type (...InvokerTransformer) to deserialize: prevented for security reasons, no flag; residual(WrapperConnectionPoolDataSource)@v1 -> HTTP 200 RESULT=DESERIALIZED com.mchange.v2.c3p0.WrapperConnectionPoolDataSource, PCB_CANARY_FLAG echoed (residual reaches PAST the 7525 fix -- the enumerated 2.8.9 blacklist omits this name); residual@v2 -> HTTP 200 RESULT=BLOCKED Illegal type (...WrapperConnectionPoolDataSource) to deserialize: prevented for security reasons, no flag (name added by #1737 in 2.8.10); original@v2 -> HTTP 200 RESULT=BLOCKED (name retained), no flag. Gate via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2`: reach@v0=true, blocked@v1=true, bypass_reach@v1=true => passed=true; residual_blocked@v2=true, original_blocked@v2=true. DATA-QUALITY: distinct fixed versions (2.8.9 vs 2.8.10), distinct commits (#1599 vs #1680+#1737); V1=2.8.9 genuinely has the CVE-2017-7525 guard (InvokerTransformer BLOCKED, NOT the V1-had-no-guard failure) and is genuinely bypassed by the residual it does not cover; V2 closes exactly that residual; original != residual on V1 (InvokerTransformer BLOCKED vs WrapperConnectionPoolDataSource DESERIALIZED); V1 does not block the residual.
